post.caption:
A cold cloud with a slightly denser patch collapses under gravity, and whatever faint spin it had speeds up as it shrinks, exactly like a skater pulling their arms in. That spin flattens it: sideways orbits survive, straight-in motion cancels out. So the cloud becomes a disc, which is why our solar system lies almost in one plane. The centre compresses until fusion starts, and out in the disc dust sticks into pebbles, rocks and worlds. We can photograph it happening right now.

That is 180 days. Start again from day one, it reads completely differently.
